title: Payments and E-Money Compliance
summary: A ten-module programme giving payment and e-money firms the practical tools to meet safeguarding, fraud, financial crime and resilience expectations.
intro: This training programme equips payment and e-money firms to meet authorisation, safeguarding, operational, fraud and financial crime requirements, and to prepare for new payment rails, stablecoins and wind-down scrutiny.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give payment and e-money firms a practical understanding of the rules and supervisory expectations that apply to their business, from authorisation and safeguarding to fraud and wind-down. Participants leave able to strengthen their controls, evidence compliance and see their payments business the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: Authorisation and the regulatory perimeter, safeguarding, governance and capital, operational and security risk, fraud and authorised push payment scams, AML/CFT and sanctions, agents and distributors, open banking, wind-down planning, and stablecoins and new payment rails.
Intended Audience: Compliance officers, MLROs and risk managers at payment institutions and e-money issuers
Finance, operations, safeguarding and fraud teams responsible for day-to-day controls
Directors, senior managers and founders of payment and fintech firms
Learning Objectives: Explain the regulatory framework and authorisation requirements for payment and e-money firms
Design and evidence robust safeguarding arrangements
Assess governance, capital, operational and security risk controls
Implement fraud, AML/CFT and sanctions controls suited to payment business models
Oversee agents, distributors and open banking arrangements effectively
Prepare a credible wind-down plan and assess the impact of new payment rails
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, group exercises and practical templates, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of payments, e-money or compliance is helpful. No prior knowledge of specific payment services rules is required.
Core Reading: CPMI, Fast Payments: Enhancing the Speed and Availability of Retail Payments (2016)
FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
CPMI and World Bank, Payment Aspects of Financial Inclusion (2016)

modules.title: Authorisation and the Regulatory Perimeter
modules.summary: The main categories of payment and e-money business, how firms determine which permissions they need, and what the authority looks for in a strong application.
objectives: Distinguish payment institution, e-money and other payment business models
Map the firm's activities to the regulatory perimeter and exclusions
Prepare an authorisation application that anticipates supervisory concerns
syllabus: Payment services, e-money issuance and their regulatory treatment
Perimeter questions: exclusions, commercial agents and limited networks
Capital, business plans and the programme of operations
Common weaknesses in payment and e-money applications

modules.title: Safeguarding Customer Funds
modules.summary: Why safeguarding is the single most important customer protection in payments, the methods available and how firms design, reconcile and audit their arrangements.
objectives: Explain the purpose and methods of safeguarding
Design safeguarding reconciliations and controls
Prepare for safeguarding audits and supervisory reviews
syllabus: Segregation, insurance and guarantee methods
Relevant funds, timing and designated safeguarding accounts
Daily reconciliations, breaks and escalation
Safeguarding audits, attestations and failures in insolvency

modules.title: Governance, Capital and Fitness
modules.summary: The governance, risk management and capital arrangements a payment or e-money firm needs, and how boards and senior managers evidence sound oversight.
objectives: Assess governance arrangements against supervisory expectations
Calculate and monitor own funds and capital requirements
Apply fitness and propriety standards to directors and key function holders
syllabus: Board composition, control functions and three lines of defence
Own funds calculations, capital planning and liquidity
Fitness and propriety of directors and qualifying holders
Management information and regulatory reporting

modules.title: Operational, Security and Third-Party Risk
modules.summary: How payment firms manage operational and security risk, including incident reporting, strong customer authentication, outsourcing and reliance on technology providers.
objectives: Design an operational and security risk management framework
Implement strong customer authentication and incident reporting
Manage outsourcing and third-party risk, including cloud and banking partners
syllabus: Operational and security risk assessments and controls
Strong customer authentication and its exemptions
Major incident management and reporting to the authority
Outsourcing, banking partners, cloud and concentration risk

modules.title: Fraud and Authorised Push Payment Scams
modules.summary: How payment fraud and authorised push payment scams work, the controls that prevent them, and emerging approaches to reimbursement and liability sharing.
objectives: Recognise payment fraud and scam typologies
Design fraud prevention, detection and customer warning controls
Apply reimbursement, liability and data-sharing arrangements
syllabus: Fraud typologies: account takeover, impersonation and investment scams
Transaction monitoring, confirmation of payee and effective warnings
Reimbursement, liability sharing and vulnerable customers
Fraud data, intelligence sharing and AI-enabled detection

modules.title: AML/CFT and Sanctions in Payments
modules.summary: The financial crime risks specific to payment and e-money firms and how to build a risk-based AML/CFT and sanctions framework aligned with FATF standards.
objectives: Assess money laundering and terrorist financing risks in payments
Design customer due diligence, monitoring and travel rule controls
Implement sanctions screening for payments and customers
syllabus: Business-wide risk assessment for payment and e-money models
Customer due diligence, simplified due diligence and e-money thresholds
Transaction monitoring, payment transparency and suspicious activity reporting
Sanctions screening, payment filtering and money mule risk

modules.title: Agents, Distributors and Partners
modules.summary: How firms oversee agents, distributors and programme partners who act on their behalf, and remain responsible for their compliance and conduct.
objectives: Explain the firm's responsibility for agents and distributors
Design onboarding, registration and monitoring of agents and distributors
Assess risks in embedded finance and partner programmes
syllabus: Agents versus distributors: roles and regulatory treatment
Due diligence, registration and fitness of agents
Ongoing monitoring, audits and termination
Embedded finance, programme managers and white-label models

modules.title: Open Banking and Customer Outcomes
modules.summary: How account information and payment initiation services work, the obligations of providers and account holders, and how to deliver fair outcomes for payment customers.
objectives: Explain account information and payment initiation services
Assess API access, consent and data protection obligations
Evaluate customer outcomes, complaints and disclosure in payments
syllabus: Account information and payment initiation services
Dedicated interfaces, consent and data sharing
Fees, transparency and information requirements
Complaints handling and redress

modules.title: Wind-Down Planning and Resolution
modules.summary: How payment and e-money firms prepare for an orderly wind-down that returns customer funds promptly, and what supervisors expect to see in a credible plan.
objectives: Design a credible wind-down plan and trigger framework
Identify the resources and dependencies needed for an orderly exit
Test the plan and integrate it with safeguarding and recovery arrangements
syllabus: Wind-down triggers, indicators and governance
Returning customer funds and insolvency considerations
Critical staff, systems, partners and costs of exit
Testing, review and board approval

modules.title: Stablecoins and New Payment Rails
modules.summary: Brings the programme together with the developments reshaping payments: instant payments, stablecoins, tokenised deposits and agentic payments, closing with a compliance action plan.
objectives: Explain how instant payments, stablecoins and tokenised deposits work
Assess the regulatory and risk implications of new payment rails
Produce a payments compliance action plan
syllabus: Instant payments and settlement risk
Stablecoins, e-money tokens and tokenised deposits under regional crypto-asset regimes
Agentic payments and programmable money
Workshop: seeing the payments business the way a supervisor does

related.title: EU Payments Regulation: PSD2, PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on EU payments regulation for supervisors and firms, covering PSD2 and EMD2 today and the PSD3 and Payment Services Regulation reform package.

related.title: Crypto-Asset Compliance Programme
related.summary: An advanced twelve-module programme for compliance, risk and MLRO staff at crypto-asset service providers, from authorisation and custody to market abuse, AML/CFT and wind-down.

related.title: Digital Operational Resilience under DORA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on DORA for supervisors and financial entities: ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and TLPT, ICT third-party risk and critical provider oversight.

related.title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.

related.title: Governance, Risk and Compliance for Market Infrastructures
related.summary: A ten-module programme for boards, managers and control functions of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs and payment systems on meeting the PFMI in governance, risk, default management and recovery.

related.title: Investment Services Compliance
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving compliance and risk staff at investment firms the tools to build, test and evidence compliance across the client journey and market activity.
